title: Vienna Game: the ideas
line: The knight comes out first, and the pawn on f2 is ready to push.

steps.text: In the Vienna Game White brings the queen side knight out first. The pawn on f2 stays free to push, as in the King's Gambit.
Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to c3. It guards your pawn on e4 and keeps the way clear for the pawn on f2.

also.g1f3: The other knight is the most common move, also sound, and leads to other openings. This lesson brings this knight out.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.text: Push the pawn on f2 two squares. It attacks the pawn on e5. Engines rate this push about level.

also.f1c4: The bishop move is also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.g2g3: Making room for the bishop on the long diagonal is also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.g1f3: That leads to the Four Knights Game, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.after: Black takes, as many club players do. Masters strike back in the center instead: the next lesson.

steps.text: That take is a slip: push the pawn on e4 one square. It attacks the knight, which has only one safe square.
steps.after: The knight goes all the way back home.

steps.text: Bring your other knight out. It keeps the black queen from checking on h4.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. Your pawns hold the center.

also.d1e2: That is also played. This lesson builds the center.

steps.after: You take back on e5 next, and later the pawn on f4. Meanwhile your pieces are out and Black's are at home.

summary: The knight out first guards the center pawn and leaves the side pawn free to push. If Black takes it, chase the knight.
